verdict.probe_answer: Both arms add a classifier-level signal distinct from 'type resolved': Arm A via a 3-state enum (Unmaterialized/MaterializedPoisoned/Recovered) computed from whether receiver_type_in_fn syntactically recovered a typed-param/constructor-local/annotated-local shape; Arm B via a materialized bool set independently inside the AST walk itself (survives the bindings>1 shadow-bail, arguably slightly more general). Both correctly gate R3/R3b suppression to Python/JS/TS and route poisoned bindings to R6 residue. Both reproduce all 3 repros with regression tests that would fail pre-fix (old gate was site.receiver_type.is_some()). Key divergence: Arm A scopes the byte-vs-line 'binding before call' cutoff strictly to Python/JS/TS (byte_scoped flag), leaving Rust/Go on the original line check — matching the spec's explicit 'Rust/Go byte-identical' directive. Arm B replaced call_line with call_start_byte universally in receiver_type_in_fn/walk_receiver_bindings, changing the cutoff semantics for Rust/Go too (low real-world impact given declare-before-use semantics, but a genuine spec deviation). Arm A's class-body skip also covers TS abstract_class_declaration; Arm B's does not, missing a demonstrable nested-class-body case for abstract classes. Arm A's tests are more rigorous (wildcard-import variant, JS nested-class-body test, explicit receiver_materialized + NameOnly-residue assertions); Arm B tests only the plain-poison Python variant and only a Python nested-class case, with weaker assertions (absence of Exact QualifierOwner only, no residue-confidence check).
verdict.rationale: Both arms correctly implement the core BLOCKER fix (materialized-vs-resolved state) and MAJOR fix (byte-precise + class-scope-aware recovery), and both add TDD tests for all three repros plus a positive control, satisfying the brief's letter. Arm A is materially better on two concrete, demonstrable points: (1) it strictly gates the byte-cutoff change to Python/JS/TS, honoring the explicit 'Rust/Go byte-identical' instruction, while Arm B applies the byte cutoff universally including Rust/Go (SMELL: unrequested blast-radius expansion, low real-world impact but a real deviation); (2) Arm A's class-body skip includes TS abstract_class_declaration, which Arm B omits — a concrete input (`abstract class C { x = new Foo(); }` nested in a function, followed by `x.m()`) reproduces the exact MAJOR-class bug under Arm B but not Arm A. Arm A's tests are also broader and more rigorous (tests both Python and JS nested-class-body repro forms per the spec's plural framing, tests both import- and wildcard-poisoned Python variants, and explicitly asserts the required NameOnly/residue routing rather than only the absence of the wrong Exact kind). Arm B's alternative design (tracking materialized independently through the recursive walk, surviving the bindings>1 shadow-bail) is a legitimate, arguably more principled architectural choice, but it's untested/unrequested and doesn't offset the concrete scope and coverage gaps. Neither arm shows a demonstrated-broken required repro (no true WRONG against the 3 mandated fixes), so this is a quality/thoroughness edge, not a correctness failure, for Arm B.
